Understanding How a One Search Strategy Works

The One Search approach aims to optimize overall performance by combining organic (SEO) and paid (SEM) levers around the same priority keyword territories. The goal is to maximize coverage of search intent — branded and non-branded — while intelligently arbitrating investment between the two channels.

🎯 Identify priority keywords

Select strategic branded and non-branded keywords with high volume and high conversion potential.

🔧 Optimize on-site content

Technical fixes, metadata and editorial content optimization to strengthen organic relevance.

⭐ Improve SEM Quality Score

Align landing pages with search intent to improve QS, reduce CPC and improve conversion rate.

👑 SERP Domination

Secure top SEO + SEM positions on branded queries to maximize share of voice and prevent competitive capture.

🌱 SEO/SEM Arbitrage

Prioritize SEM where SEO is absent from page 1. Gradually reduce SEM as SEO reaches top 3.

📋 Production plan

SEM A/B tests on RSAs and LPs to identify winning combinations before scaling. SEO Quick Wins first (Title, Meta, internal linking) on high-conversion-potential keywords.

Data Analyzed & Coverage Methodology

The OneSearch audit analyzes 6 dimensions for each keyword and category, from demand through to conversion.

1 · Demand

Monthly search volume per keyword — reference baseline for measuring coverage and identifying opportunities.

2 · Impressions

Number of appearances in the SERPs (SEO + SEM). Compared to search potential to evaluate raw coverage.

3 · Clicks

Traffic generated from organic and paid results. Measures the real impact of ads and optimized pages.

4 · Conversions

Transformation of search traffic into actions (purchases, leads). Compares performance by category and channel.

5 · Coverage

Understanding actual search audience coverage, based on your SEM and SEO data.

6 · Cost

SEM advertising spend (actual Google Ads cost) and SEO valuation via market CPCs — to measure budget efficiency per channel.

Coverage is the central metric of a One Search strategy: it measures the share of the Search audience actually captured relative to total market demand. Its reliability relies on Google Keyword Planner volumes, which incorporate the actual seasonality of searches — providing an objective market baseline, independent of internal performance fluctuations. High coverage means the brand effectively occupies the Search territory across all surfaces.

SEO Coverage

Σ SEO Clicks / Σ Search Volume

SEM Coverage

Σ SEM Clicks / Σ Search Volume

OneSearch Coverage

(Σ SEO Clicks + Σ SEM Clicks) / Σ Search Volume

SEO Cost

Avg. CPC × SEO Clicks
Note on volumes: A keyword is counted in the SEO volume only if it generates at least 1 SEO click during the period. Same logic for SEM. A keyword active on both channels contributes to both volumes without duplication in OneSearch.
SEM Qualified Visit (QV) Methodology

Starting Q1 2026, SEM Qualified Visits are calculated using a landing-page pro-rata attribution method applied to the GA4 Google Ads session export. This aligns SEM QV measurement with the existing SEO QV methodology.

Source: GA4 Google Ads session export — tab Campagnes Google Ads: Requête Google Ads associée à cette session. Covers Jan 1 – Mar 31, 2026. Key Events = MikMak Checkout events = Qualified Visits.

Step 1 — LP QV Rate

LP Key Events / LP Sessions

Step 2 — Keyword Attribution

(Keyword Sessions / LP Total Sessions) × LP Total Key Events

Step 3 — Sum Across LPs

Σ Attributed QV across all Landing Pages per keyword

Verification

Σ Keyword QV SEM ≈ Total Key Events in GA4 export
Q1 2026 result: 1,338 total SEM QVs attributed across 1,863 matched keywords (out of 3,663 in the keyword spine). 70 QVs are from search queries not yet in the spine — flagged for next spine expansion. Attribution delta vs GA4 total: 0.0 (verified).
Metrics Glossary
Metric Definition
Volume (Demand)Estimated monthly searches on Google for a given keyword, on the US market.
Coverage OneSearchShare of search volume captured via SEO or SEM during the current period. Key indicator of overall SERP presence.
Coverage SEOShare of volume captured exclusively via organic traffic, for keywords with at least 1 SEO click.
Coverage SEMShare of volume captured exclusively via paid traffic, for keywords with at least 1 SEM click.
Clicks OneSearchTotal clicks generated via organic results and paid ads on Google Search.
Impressions OneSearchTotal number of SERP appearances across all positions, organic and paid.
SEO ClicksClicks generated from organic results during the Q1 2026 period (Jan.–Mar.).
SEM ClicksClicks generated from paid ads on the Google Search Network, Q1 2026 period.
SEO ImpressionsNumber of times the URL was displayed in organic results during the analyzed period.
SEM ImpressionsNumber of times the ad was displayed in paid results during the analyzed period.
CTR SEOOrganic click-through rate — measures the attractiveness of the organic result (title, meta, rich snippets).
CTR SEMPaid click-through rate — measures the relevance and attractiveness of ads.
Conversions (Qualify Visits)Number of qualified visits attributed to the Search channel during the period. Includes SEO and SEM separately. A Qualify Visit corresponds to a session with significant engagement on the site.
QV SEOQualified Visits attributed to organic search. Source: GA4 MikMak Checkout key events joined to GSC keyword data via landing page URL.
QV SEMQualified Visits attributed to paid search. Calculated via landing-page pro-rata attribution from the GA4 Google Ads session export (Q1 2026, new methodology). Formula: (Keyword SEM Sessions / LP Total SEM Sessions) × LP Total Key Events, summed across all landing pages per keyword.
SEM CostTotal advertising spend on Google Ads for the category's keywords during the analyzed period.
Qualify Visit (QV)Qualified session with significant engagement on the Oikos site. Primary conversion metric used to evaluate Search channel performance (SEO and SEM). Replaces revenue in a non-e-commerce context.
Avg. CPCAverage cost per click paid on Google Search ads. Directly dependent on Quality Score.
Conversions SEO / SEMNumber of qualifying actions (purchases, add-to-cart, leads) generated via each channel.
Quality Score (QS)Score from 1 to 10 assigned by Google to each SEM keyword. Directly impacts CPC and Ad Rank. Components: expected CTR, ad relevance, LP experience.
Landing Page ExperienceAssessment of the relevance and user experience of the landing page relative to the keyword. Component of Quality Score.
SEO PositionAverage Google Search Console Q1 2026 position per keyword. Ranking data also sourced from SE Ranking tool (December 2025). In the SQR table, individual position per keyword. In Recommendations, average position for the sub-category. Colors: green ≤ 3 · orange ≤ 10 · grey > 10.
Current PeriodQ1 2026: January 1 to March 31, 2026. Reference data for all primary KPIs.
Previous PeriodQ4 2025: October 1 to December 31, 2025. Used to calculate changes (▲▼ %) displayed in the dashboard.
Keyword Classification Guide

Each keyword in the OneSearch study is classified into a territory (TOPICS), a category, and a sub-category. The territory is the primary filter used throughout the dashboard.

1
BRANDBranded / Navigational
Keywords that explicitly name the Oikos brand, product lines (Triple Zero, Pro, Fusion, Remix), or brand variants (misspellings, parent company). The highest-intent territory — users already know the brand.
oikosoikos triple zerooikos pro drinkableoikos protein shakeoikos flip
2
PRODUCTCommercial / Transactional
Generic product-type keywords — protein shakes, Greek yogurt, drinkable yogurt — where Oikos is a natural answer but the brand is not mentioned. Captures shoppers in product discovery or comparison mode.
protein shakehigh protein Greek yogurtdrinkable yogurtready-to-drink protein
3
COMPETITORCompetitive / Conquest
Keywords that name competing products or brands (Core Power, Premier Protein, Chobani, Fairlife). Oikos can capture switcher traffic and conquest clicks via SEM on these terms.
core power protein shakepremier protein shakefairlife core power
4
GENERICInformational / Top-of-funnel
Broad, non-branded category queries about protein drinks, shakes, or yogurt with no specific brand intent. High volume, high competition. Entry-point for new-to-category consumers.
best protein drinkRTD protein shakeprotein snackhigh protein snack
5
HEALTHInformational / Health-driven
Health, diet, and nutrition queries — GLP-1 diets, weight loss, high-protein nutrition — where Oikos protein content is a relevant answer. Growing territory driven by GLP-1 medication trends.
GLP-1 snackshigh protein diet planGLP-1 foodshealthy protein shake
6
SOURCE OF PROTEINInformational / Fitness-driven
Functional protein-source queries tied to fitness and muscle goals (muscle gain, building, bulking). Searched by gym-goers evaluating protein sources. Strategic long-term SEO opportunity for Oikos as a fitness brand.
protein for muscle gainprotein for muscle buildingprotein for muscle mass
7
RECIPEInformational / Content
Recipe and meal-prep queries that use Greek yogurt or protein shakes as an ingredient. Supports content SEO and positions Oikos as a versatile kitchen staple beyond direct consumption.
Greek yogurt recipeprotein shake recipebaking with Greek yogurtyogurt cake
8
CONSUMER HABITSInformational / Lifestyle
Occasion and lifestyle queries (breakfast, snack, meal prep, sports) that frame protein consumption as part of a daily routine. Useful for editorial content targeting habit-formation moments.
high protein breakfastprotein snackpost-workout protein meal
9
OTHERMixed / Miscellaneous
Miscellaneous queries including brand misspellings, customer service, promotions, and coupons. Low strategic priority but useful for brand monitoring and defensive coverage.
oikos couponoikos customer serviceoikos promo code
Coverage Status & Priority Levels

Each territory is assigned a priority status based on its OneSearch Coverage (Clicks ÷ Demand). The status drives the urgency of action and how the territory is colour-coded in the Recommendations section.

Status Coverage threshold What it means & recommended action
Coverage gap Below target
<3% non-brand
<10% brand		 The territory captures less than the coverage target. Demand exists but the brand is missing from search results. Action: Activate or scale both SEO and SEM. Prioritise these territories first — they represent the largest opportunity gap relative to demand.
Growth opportunity Approaching target
3–10% non-brand
10–25% brand		 Coverage is above the minimum threshold but below the optimal range. Momentum is building. Action: Invest in content depth and refine SEM bidding. These territories have active traffic and can reach higher coverage with focused effort in 1–2 quarters.
Maintain coverage At or above target
>10% non-brand
>25% brand		 The territory has reached its coverage target. Performance is healthy. Action: Maintain current SEO+SEM presence. Monitor competitor activity to protect positions. Avoid reducing spend without incrementality measurement — coverage can erode quickly if a competitor scales bids.

Across 9 territories and 3,662 classified keywords, Oikos USA delivered 278K OneSearch clicks in Q1 2026 — +325% vs Q4 2025 (65,541 OS clicks) — at 6.1% average coverage (+4.7pp QoQ). Coverage measures the share of total monthly search demand (5.5M searches/month) actually captured through OneSearch (SEO + SEM combined clicks ÷ Keyword Study volume). ⚠ SEM data was not available for Q4 2025 — the +325% OS lift and coverage gain are largely explained by the launch of paid campaigns in Q1 2026, not organic growth.

SEO Highlights

68K SEO clicks in Q1 2026 (+4% vs 65,541 in Q4 2025). Top SEO territory: PRODUCT (52K clicks). Q1 2026 is the first full quarter following the site migration from oikosyogurt.com → oikos.com (Oct 2025), which caused significant technical issues including a large volume of 404 errors. Pre-migration Q2 2025 traffic was ~150K organic clicks vs 68K in Q1 2026 — SEO performance has not yet recovered to pre-migration levels.

SEM Highlights

210K paid clicks in Q1 2026 (new — no SEM data for Q4 2025). Top SEM territory: PRODUCT (186K clicks). Note: Oikos USA does not currently have an active SEM contract with digitad. The SEM activity reflected here was a standalone campaign; ongoing paid support is not confirmed for Q2.

Q2 2026 Priorities
  • Optimize category and product pages to rebuild organic visibility in the PRODUCT territory
  • Focus on non-branded product search — create missing category pages for protein shakes and high-protein yogurt
  • Close coverage gaps (<3%) in: COMPETITOR, GENERIC, HEALTH
  • Complete taxonomy enrichment to classify untagged keywords
Q4 2025 SEO: 65,541 organic clicks. Q1 2026: 68,002 SEO clicks (+4% QoQ). Average coverage (6.1%) = OneSearch clicks ÷ total monthly search demand (5.5M searches in the Keyword Study) — the share of available search volume actually captured through clicks.

Context: Q1 2026 is the first full quarter following the site migration from oikosyogurt.com to oikos.com (Q4 2025). The migration triggered significant technical issues including a large number of 404 errors. Pre-migration Q2 2025 (Apr–Jun) organic traffic was ~150K clicks; Q1 2026 was 68K — SEO performance has not yet recovered to pre-migration levels.

Note: Paid search data was not available for Q4 2025. The +325% OS click jump between Q4 and Q1 is largely driven by the launch of paid campaigns in Q1 2026, not organic growth.

Q1 2026 — SEO Actions

  • SEO clicks +4% QoQ — 68K clicks vs 65,541 in Q4 2025
  • Production plan created; thorough technical audit completed; 404 errors from the oikosyogurt.com → oikos.com migration addressed
  • No new content published; no other technical recommendations implemented in Q1
  • PRODUCT: 52K SEO clicks (13.6% coverage) — lacks visibility for smoothie and shake product keywords
  • Zero SEO clicks in: SOURCE OF PROTEIN, CONSUMER HABITS — content gap

Q1 2026 — SEM Activity

Not applicable — Oikos USA does not have an active SEM contract with digitad. The 210K paid clicks reflected in Q1 2026 data are from a standalone campaign and are not part of an ongoing managed program.

Q2 2026 Pipeline — SEO

  • Q2 (To Validate / In Progress): Category pages — High Protein Drinks, High Protein Yogurt, High Protein Shakes, Remix, High Protein Greek Yogurts; Product pages — Vanilla Protein Yogurt, Vanilla Protein Shake, Vanilla Protein Drink (Fusion), Plain & Strawberry Greek Yogurt (Triple Zero), Strawberry Banana Protein Drink (Pro), Salted Caramel & Chocolate Shakes, Pro range product pages; Recipes: Strawberry Banana Smoothie, Strawberry Mango Smoothie
  • Off-site: guest posts in progress anchoring high protein greek yogurt, protein drink, high protein shake to category pages — DA 40–77 domains
  • Focus on non-branded search traffic — GENERIC and HEALTH territories undercaptured (<1% coverage); continue technical cleanup from the oikos.com migration

Q2 2026 Pipeline — SEM

  • Align Q2 ad groups with top-converting Q1 search terms to maximize qualified visits per dollar spent
  • Improve brand impression share through two levers: (1) add the 17 identified negative keywords where SEM QV = 0 and SEO coverage >10% — budget freed should be reallocated to high-QV terms; (2) increase bid strategy on keywords generating strong qualified visits and solid organic SEO performance to capture incremental demand from users already showing purchase intent. Monitor landing page performance (qualified visit rate by LP) to inform bid prioritization.
  • Explore SEO and SEM synergies across the Danone North America portfolio — coordinate keyword strategy and share learnings on high-QV sub-categories

PRODUCT — Q2 #1 Priority: Non-Branded Visibility Gap
SEO+SEMPRODUCTQ2
Overall territory coverage 14% (above target), but that average is skewed by strong branded performance. Non-branded sub-categories — protein shakes, Oikos Pro, protein drinks (Fusion) — have very low visibility in the evaluate and buy portions of the funnel. SEO: 52K · SEM: 186K clicks in Q1 2026.
  • Highest Q2 priority. Optimize existing product pages and create missing category pages to capture non-branded evaluate-stage intent. Oikos Triple Zero performs well for high protein yogurt; other product ranges (Pro, Fusion/protein drinks, Remix) lack visibility.
  • Q2 production plan (To Validate / In Progress): Category pages — High Protein Drinks, High Protein Yogurt, High Protein Shakes, Remix, High Protein Greek Yogurts (Triple Zero). Product pages — Vanilla Protein Yogurt, Vanilla Protein Shake, Vanilla Protein Drink (Fusion), Plain & Strawberry Greek Yogurt (Triple Zero), Strawberry Banana Protein Drink (Pro), Salted Caramel & Chocolate Shakes, Pro range. Q3–Q4: smoothie, drinkable yogurt sub-categories.
08
BRAND — Maintain coverage
SEO+SEMBRAND
Coverage at 29% — above target. Maintain SEO+SEM dual presence. Monitor competitor activity and protect top positions. SEO: 15K · SEM: 1.1K clicks in Q1 2026.
09
OTHER — Maintain coverage
SEO
Coverage at 51% — above target. Maintain SEO+SEM dual presence. Monitor competitor activity and protect top positions. SEO: 230 · SEM: 253 clicks in Q1 2026.
10
BRAND SEM — Add 17 negative keywords
SEMBRANDQ2
Q1 analysis identified 17 BRAND keywords where SEO coverage > 10%, SEO position ≤ 5, and SEM QV = 0 — paid clicks produce no qualified visits while organic already dominates. Adding these as negatives frees budget for higher-converting terms. See Brand SEM Campaign Optimization section below.
11
BRAND SEM — Target 80% impression share on core brand terms
SEMBRANDQ2
Target: 80% impression share for oikos, oikos triple zero, oikos pro, oikos yogurt. Brand coverage at 29% — above 10% threshold but impression share must be monitored monthly. Reallocate budget freed from negative keyword exclusions to defend core brand positions. 59 brand keywords confirmed Keep-Active with positive SEM QV.
12
BRAND SEM — Monitor 8 Keep-Test keywords (4-week rule)
SEMBRANDQ2-Q3
8 BRAND keywords flagged Keep-Test: SEO coverage > 10% but SEM is still generating qualified visits. These terms are candidates for future pausing — but require 4-week monitoring of organic clicks after any change. Track GSC organic position and SEM QV monthly. Pause only when organic traffic holds without paid support for 2 consecutive months.
13
QS IMPROVEMENT — Upgrade 7 keywords below QS 5
SEM QSALLQ2
7 keywords with QS ≤ 5 identified. Each point of QS improvement reduces CPC by ~15–20%. Priority fixes: improve landing page relevance for low-QS terms, align ad copy with search intent, ensure LP loads fast on mobile. See Quality Score tab for full list.
14
SEM QV TRACKING — Establish monthly GA4 reporting cadence
SEMALLQ2
Q1 2026 establishes the first QV SEM baseline (1,338 QVs attributed). Starting Q2: run monthly GA4 Ads export and apply LP-rate attribution methodology to track SEM qualified visit trends by keyword. Connect QV SEM data to coverage decisions (bid up on high-QV terms, add negatives on zero-QV SEO-covered terms). Update masterlist each quarter.
15
SPINE EXPANSION — Add 70 unmatched GA4 queries to keyword spine
SEMALLQ3
70 SEM QVs are attributed to search queries not yet in the keyword spine. These represent real paid conversions from untracked terms. Add to spine before Q3 reporting. Run SE Ranking API on these terms to capture volume and position data.
